text:
carmen: heads-up — after the kernel-routing change we merged earlier today, a handful of dedicated hosts reported OOMs during kv-warmup spikes. profiler + traces look noisy around allocator splits and big free lists. wondering if we should try knob tuning (expandable_segments, max_split_size_mb, garbage_collection_threshold) before rolling back :thinking_face:

ashwin: can you paste the memory_summary / allocator stats? curious whether it's fragmentation or a single huge allocation failing. also which model/batch distribution was hit in prod?

carmen: repro snapshot from one host (simplified):
```
torch.cuda.memory_summary(device=0)
Allocated: 4.8 GiB, Active: 5.2 GiB, Cached: 1.0 GiB
Largest free block: 24.5 MiB
Num segments: 58, Avg segment size: 96 MiB
Allocator stats: split_count=312, merge_count=18, expandable_segments=true
KV cache warmup pattern: many ~30-200KB allocations then large 40MB allocations for batching tails
```
Looks like lots of small allocations then a mid-size 40MB allocation fails because free blocks are fragmented.

jordana: yeah that matches what i saw in staging when batching heuristics changed — the new batch packing creates many short-lived buffers and leaves small holes. two quick ideas: 1) reduce max_split_size_mb so the allocator splits segments into smaller chunks (more usable small blocks) and 2) bump garbage_collection_threshold so GC runs earlier to coalesce freelists before the big tail alloc.

ashwin: agreed. concrete knobs I'd run in canary:
- set max_split_size_mb=64 (was 128)
- set expandable_segments=false (force splitsize strategy instead of growing segments)
- set garbage_collection_threshold=0.5 (was 0.2)
These should reduce fragmentation at the cost of slightly higher split churn. We should monitor per-token latency and iou of small-request p99.

carmen: good. any concerns about turning off expandable_segments? iirc that can increase syscalls or metadata overhead when we split a lot.

jordana: true but in this workload the tail big allocs are the pain. if expandable_segments=true we grow segments and then try to carve big contiguous blocks — but growth policy created one large segment that got sliced into tiny freebies when small allocs raced in. On balance splitting with max_split=64 should provide more consistent small blocks.

carmen: infra-bot posted the latest nightly perf snapshot — shows a small p50 cost bump but p99 drops slightly with earlier GC: https://ci.redwood/presets/alloc-profiles/3412349

infra-bot: benchmark snapshot uploaded: alloc-profiler/3412349 (contains nvprof, py-spy, and torch allocator dumps). Reaction :robot_face:

ashwin: can we run a 1% traffic canary with those env overrides? i can instrument additional tracing to capture alloc/fragmentation deltas. command to set in the canary container: 
```bash
export RW_ALLOC_MAX_SPLIT_MB=64
export RW_ALLOC_EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS=0
export RW_ALLOC_GC_THRESHOLD=0.5
./start-serving --canary=1 --tag=alloc-tune-3412349
```

jordana: also add a short-lived KV warmup job that mimics real traffic (prefix-heavy) so we stress the exact path. don't rely on cold synthetic traces.

carmen: plan: spin canary now, 2h warmup, capture memory_summary and tracer flame. if stable, roll to 10% then 50% with auto-rollback on OOM spike >3 hosts in 15m. i'll post updates here. action items: ashwin -> add tracing hooks; jordana -> kv warmup job; infra -> canary rollout.

ashwin: acked — i'll add delta metrics (largest_free_block, num_segments, fragmentation_ratio) and alert thresholds.

jordana: ack, will run warmup and post logs.

carmen: thanks — will watch and report. if we see perf regressions we can try softer values (max_split=96, gc=0.4) before rolling back the kernel change.
